Friend —
In 2000, I became a US citizen at the age of 17. It was the start of a new life in Minneapolis, and I quickly got involved in organizing in my neighborhood.
In 2016, I ran for office for the first time, winning a seat in the Minnesota State House and gaining the incredible opportunity to serve the people of Minneapolis.
In 2018, we shocked the entire political establishment when we won our race for Minnesota’s 5th congressional district, and I, along with Rashida Tlaib, became the first Muslim women ever elected to serve in Congress, as well as the first woman of color to be elected to Congress in Minnesota.
In 2020, I faced my first primary challenger as an incumbent and, despite a tough battle, we won big, earning two more years representing Minneapolis. We went on to do the same in 2022 and 2024, too, despite millions of dollars being spent to take me down and stop our progressive movement.

body:
Godly leadership or policies that ignore biblical values?
| | | | |
---
|
---
Fellow Patriot,
The Virginia governor’s race is razor-thin, with RealClearPolitics showing just a **3% difference** between the candidates in the latest poll. That margin could be as high as **95,700 votes** or as low as **82,800**. The difference between godly leadership and policies that ignore biblical values.

My name is Kendall Qualls. I wasn’t born into privilege or power. I was raised in Harlem, New York, in the 1960s; a child of divorce and one of several siblings living in public housing. Before I reached middle school, I moved to a trailer park in Oklahoma to live with my father. Neither of my parents finished high school.
I didn’t take shortcuts. I worked full-time to put myself through college. I used student loans and paid them back in full. I served as an officer in the United States Army. I earned an MBA from the University of Michigan. Then, I spent 30 years leading teams and driving innovation in the healthcare industry — rising to become Global Vice President of an $850 million business unit.
Now, I’m running for Governor of Minnesota to make sure that the principles that lifted me - hard work, faith, family, personal responsibility, and the free enterprise system - are preserved, defended, and passed on to the next generation.
We don’t need more government. We need more opportunities.

**SATIRE OP-ED | Nation Faces Shutdown, War, Dodgers Playoff Drama—and Congress Hurls Itself at... a Ballroom?**
_By Dominic Rapini - American Businessman, Political Commentator, and proud American of Italian Descent_
**WASHINGTON, D.C.** — In a stunning show of legislative priorities, American politicians and activists have, as of this week, abandoned silly distractions like government shutdowns, runaway inflation, and the small matter of a war in Ukraine in favor of that gravest threat to the republic: **President Trump’s sinister plot to let future presidents dance.**
Yes, America, while the world burns, Washington’s hottest fight isn’t about securing the border, passing a budget, or figuring out who’s responsible for printers at the DMV. No, patriotic Americans are taking up arms—be they Twitter threads or recycled protest signs—against the first major White House renovation in a generation: a privately-funded, 90,000-square-foot ballroom, intended to replace the undersized East Wing.
**Outraged House Democrats have gathered in emergency session,** vowing to protect the American people from private donations, large spaces, and—worst of all—elegant galas. Leading the charge: Congressman Eric Swalwell, who, having solved all other national problems, has now announced that any 2028 Democrat “worth their salt” must campaign on a sacred wrecking ball pledge: “If elected, I vow to destroy this room of dancing, feasting, and bipartisan dialogue—because it’s**making President Trump happy, and that’s simply un-American.”**
Talk about cultural enrichment. We used to envy Russian-style political intrigue—now we just envy their focus.
Pundits have tried desperately to stoke outrage, swearing the American people will not stand for a charitable ballroom, no matter how elegant or financially responsible. “If this isn’t the hill to die on, what is?” said an unnamed strategist, pocketing a fundraising check labeled “Save Democracy: Ban Waltzing.” Meanwhile, repaired bridges, Social Security, and the ongoing LA Dodgers–Toronto Blue Jays World Series—far too trivial for peak outrage—continue without **congressional foot-stomping or demands for dramatic bulldozers.**
Let’s look at the facts few care to shout about: Every president for over a century has overseen White House renovations, mostly with taxpayer dollars. Teddy Roosevelt invented the West Wing, Truman rebuilt the whole thing, FDR added the East Wing, JFK upgraded the art. **But President Trump gets private funding (and even chips in millions of his own money), and suddenly it’s a crisis for democracy?** If only the Founders knew adding a ballroom was the death knell for the republic, perhaps they’d have written an anti-foxtrot clause in the Bill of Rights. Still, Democratic strategists say the party needs this issue. “Look,” one staffer admitted, “we tried running on ‘Healthcare for All’ and people asked about dental. With the ballroom, you just point and scream, ‘GAH, OPULENCE!’ and hope nobody remembers Obama spent $376 million fixing the West Portico just to keep the pigeons out.”
Critics note that the ballroom will be the only event space in the White House capable of holding over 1,000 guests (if you don’t count the Rose Garden, which is mostly for tulips and press gaggles). Historic state dinners, bipartisan compromise summits, even the annual Shameless Ball for Out-of-Work Cable News Hosts—finally, all could be truly “presidential.” But why invest in the dignity of the executive branch, when you can leave major events to cramped parlors or, better yet, the Four Seasons Landscaping parking lot?
Meanwhile, north of the border, Canadians reportedly look on with envy. “A ballroom? You folks realize Justin Trudeau hosts G7 dinners in his mom’s garage,” said one Ottawa resident, stoking the wood stove to fend off mid-May frostbite. “Heck, our last state function ended in a log-rolling contest and a hockey brawl.” If Congress gets its way, the White House will remain mired in ballroom-less mediocrity. **“Let the British host banquets at Buckingham, let Paris light up the Élysée—Americans will simply host world leaders in the Lincoln Bedroom... or, failing that, Zoom.”**
Incredibly, this is happening while Americans face rising prices, international crises, and, far more importantly, wonder whether the Dodgers can finish off those tariff-hating Blue Jays in four games or struggle to five. **Canadians, of course, would walk barefoot through a snowstorm for a taste of such luxury** ; all they have is maple syrup, universal healthcare, and a government that can’t afford even decent ballroom flooring. “We’d kill for a full-sized ballroom,” confided a Toronto native. “Our last one was commandeered as a moose shelter.”
Back in Washington, Defenders of Common Sense prepare to go down swinging. “We will not be distracted,” announced an anonymous White House staffer between arranging caviar trays. “There’s a future to win, a country to run, and—more relevantly—a new venue for Fox & Friends to host their annual disco charity ball.”
**So here’s a plea to lawmakers: maybe, just maybe, save the outrage for genuine priorities, like budget deadlines—or, more realistically, high-stakes baseball. After all, you can always threaten to bulldoze the ballroom later, when Americans care even less.**
**#BallroomGate #EastWingSwag #DancingWithThePresidents #HistoricRenovationRumble #ByeByeBunker #TaxpayerFreeTango #NoMoreCoatRoom #OvalOfficeWaltz #PresidentialPartyPalace #LetThemEatCaviar #WhiteHouseGlowUp #NorthWingJealousy #CanadiansWantABallroomToo**

|
---
|
---
| |

**Precious White House Artifacts Lost to History (Satire)**
• First Lady’s Emergency Tiara Cabinet: Where generations of First Ladies stored their backup tiaras for surprise state dinners and ballroom emergencies.
• The White House Family Theater’s Original Velvet Seats: Rumored to be stuffed with classified documents and popcorn from the Ford era.
• The Presidential Emergency Flip-Flop Collection: Cheney wore these in the bunker—ideal for swift evacuation and comfort during historic crises.
• Caramelized Portrait of Millard Fillmore: Once displayed between Laura Bush and Hillary Clinton, accidentally left too close to the Kennedy Garden heating lamp.
• Jacqueline Kennedy’s Official Rose Clippers: Used to tame the East Garden but last seen at a staff “secret garden party” with Lyndon Johnson.
• Original East Colonnade Cloakroom: Where presidents hung their coats and hopes during bipartisan summits nobody remembers.
• 1991 White House Calligraphy Set: Responsible for decades of perfectly scribed invitations and passive-aggressive thank-you notes sent to foreign dignitaries.
• Lady Bird Johnson’s Secret Plant Mister: Allegedly kept the garden (and debate about garden names) alive for half a century.
• The Presidential Rec Room Ping Pong Table: Where Nixon lost to Carter, sparking a cold war within a war.
• The Secret Red Christmas Tree of Melania Trump: The only decoration ever accused of an “outer-space mood” by CNN, now lost to history and, possibly, an intergalactic trade agreement.
_Who knows what treasures tomorrow’s presidents will be forced to do without, now that a grand ballroom stands ready to receive dignitaries and not, apparently, spare tiaras or caramelized Millard Fillmores. America mourns. America shrugs. America, at least, will soon have somewhere with decent chairs._

I served our nation in the US Marine Corps as an electrician & a diesel mechanic. I kept my brothers & sisters on the move and equipped to DEFEND our nation from terrorists & communists. It was during my service that I learned what real leadership and sacrifice are. _**I am forever grateful that I had the privilege to serve and defend our nation, Fellow American.**_

There's a saying: _Once a Marine, always a Marine._ Every Marine shares the same spirit of duty and service that inspired me to join--to defend our neighbors and our nation. That's why, today, I'm still serving my country.

But now, I'm fighting for my friends' and neighbors' freedoms as a civilian. In 2021, I decided to run for Lieutenant Governor of Virginia because I saw that our nation needed a strong Christian, someone who has served this great country, to step up and LEAD!

**And after a historic and hard-fought battle, my team and I won by LESS THAN 1.6% of the vote!!** Now, Democrats want me _GONE_. It doesn't matter that I'm a patriotic Marine, a strong Christian, and a mom & grandma; _the Left can 't stand me because I am a proud and unapologetic conservative!_

Space Command supports more than 1,400 jobs in Colorado Springs and has a $1 billion impact on our economy. subject: How we’ll put your $20.25 contribution to work:
body:
Think about your friends or relatives who don’t always vote.
---
Derek, We wanted to send a quick note about the contributions we've received at the DNC this year, share a bit about how that money has been spent, and ask you to make your first contribution today, as Election Day rapidly approaches. This year, the DNC has invested over _$7 million_ in getting out the vote in states like Virginia, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania. But our work doesn’t end there. Think about the friends or relatives you have who don’t always vote. There are _millions_ of people just like them, in communities all over the country. In these final days before Election Day, it’s our job to reach those people. It’s up to us to get in contact with them, communicate the stakes, make sure they know what’s on their ballot, and persuade them to show up at the polls. As you can imagine, that work isn’t easy — and we rely heavily on grassroots contributions to fund it. That’s why we’re asking for a chance to earn your first contribution of 2025. Well, it’s an understatement to say there’s a lot going on right now.
Our President treating the National Guard as his personal Royal Guard.
A prolonged federal government shutdown forcing hundreds of thousands of workers to go without pay.
The illegal suspension of SNAP benefits that will put more than 41 million Americans at risk of going hungry as we head into the holidays.
Trump weaponizing the US DOJ to target his perceived enemies with baseless charges.
In short, we are facing staggering and unprecedented abuses of power — and an administration that not only refuses to rein Trump in, but actively enables and furthers his worst impulses to violate the Constitution and the law.
As your Attorney General, I’m fighting back with every ounce of power and platform I’ve got. I’ve filed 45 lawsuits against Trump in just 40 weeks, and I’m not slowing down anytime soon.
But I want to make sure I’m prioritizing the fights that matter most to you, so I’m asking for some feedback.
Will you fill out my quick end-of-month survey to let me know what’s top of mind for you? It only takes a minute, but it helps my team figure out where to focus our efforts in the weeks and months ahead. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/zaDuOGccnUa-yQwxYNoZAw2]
TAKE THE SURVEY → [https://secure.ngpvan.com/zaDuOGccnUa-yQwxYNoZAw2]
When Trump and his allies throw everything at the wall — chaos, confusion, and cruelty — we have to respond with clarity and determination.
Whether that’s arguing our cases in the courtroom, clawing back much-needed federal funding for California, or defending the right to healthcare, education, and reproductive freedom — every decision we make starts with listening.
So before October ends, will you take a minute to share what’s most important to you right now? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/zaDuOGccnUa-yQwxYNoZAw2]
Thanks for being part of this team. I really appreciate your partnership in these fights!
—Rob

Faith without votes is dead

**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
🚨 Stay tuned — The second half of the **Douglas County Dirty Dozen** drops this Friday!

Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** [Heidi Ganahl’s “DougCo Dirty Dozen”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) series put union power under the spotlight ahead of Douglas County elections, fueling parent-led calls for transparency and reform. At CU Boulder, [a TPUSA student leader](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) alleges a hockey-stick assault was politically motivated, sparking debate over campus safety and free expression. [Former Libertarian chair Hannah Goodman](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) announced she’s joining the Democratic Party as a “Truman Democrat” focused on working-class voters. And in Telluride, voters will weigh a 5% lift-ticket tax to fund the “free” gondola, a $64 million housing bond, and a [“Let the People Decide” proposal](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) requiring public votes on major developments.
🇺🇸 **On the National Stage...** Declassified Senate documents reignited scrutiny of the [DOJ’s “Arctic Frost” probe](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) targeting Donald Trump and allies after January 6. Emails show top Biden officials—including Merrick Garland, Lisa Monaco, and Christopher Wray—approved the inquiry, while the White House allegedly coordinated with an anti-Trump FBI agent to seize phones from Trump and Mike Pence. Meanwhile, [a new Democratic report](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) warns that far-left ideology has “wrecked” the party’s brand, alienating working-class and Hispanic voters and urging a return to practical, kitchen-table issues.
🗣️ **Commentary Spotlight...** Bernie Lake's “[Faith Without Votes Is Dead](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)” argues that Christian conviction must translate into political courage. Michael Hancock's “[The Marxist Roots of America’s Racial Unrest](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)” traces identity politics to century-old ideology dividing Americans by class and race. Robyn Carnes' “[Walking Together for Centennial’s Future](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)” spotlights five conservative candidates walking 500 miles to reconnect with their community. And The Gazette’s “[Colorado’s Teachers Turn Away From Unions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)” highlights the majority of teachers opting for professional independence over politicized union control.
This is the Mountain Minute for Wednesday, October 29, 2025.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Faith without votes is dead](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY BERNIE LAKE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)

_Christians should engage in the public square. Unfortunately many are unengaged, likely because there’s been a perceived disconnect between the secular and the sacred. But, there is not. Not only is voting in our elections a civic duty, it should be an act shaped by our Christian values._
_Engaging in the political process to elect our leaders, who make our laws, allows Christians to advocate for the issues that matter most to our families, our communities and should uphold biblical principles in governance._
_Often churches and pastors do not know where to start or how to shepherd their congregation in the public square. Truth and Liberty voter guides are a great place to start. They are non-partisan, and the result of biblically-based questions sent to all candidates. They are designed to inform the Christian voter where the candidate stands on these cultural issues from a Christian perspective._
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Former Colorado Libertarian Chair Crosses Over to Democratic Party](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Former Colorado Libertarian Party chair Hannah Goodman has joined the Democratic Party just days after completing her term, saying she wants to restore balance in state politics and push Democrats to return to their “historic principles” of supporting working-class and rural Americans.
* Goodman described herself as a “Truman Democrat” and said her decision was both personal and strategic—an effort to “mix up the landscape” in Republican-dominated rural Colorado by promoting liberty, fiscal restraint, and coalition-building within the Democratic Party.
* Goodman said she avoided the Republican Party because it’s “eating itself” and “can’t coalesce,” contrasting that with Democrats, whom she called “solid coalition builders.”

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

**[CU Boulder Conservative Student Says Hockey Stick Attack Was Politically Motivated](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [BOULDER DAILY CAMERA](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* CU Boulder student Nathaniel Ellis, a Turning Point USA leader, was struck in the head with a hockey stick by a masked skater who shouted “fascist,” an assault he believes was politically motivated.
* Prior to the attack, Antifa-linked social media accounts had labeled Ellis a “Nazi activist” and encouraged harassment, prompting him to report escalating threats.
* Boulder Police are investigating both the physical assault and the online harassment as potentially connected incidents; the suspect remains at large.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[The Marxist roots of America’s racial unrest](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY MICHAEL HANCOCK | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 28** _In October 1928, the Communist International — the Moscow-based command center for global revolution — issued an extraordinary directive. Buried in the archives of the Political Secretariat of the Communist International, the document was titled “Resolution on the Negro Question in the United States.” It did not read like a humanitarian plea to end racial injustice. It read like a military plan._
**[Walking Together for Centennial’s Future](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY ROBYN CARNES | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 28** _Five candidates. Over 500 miles walked. One vision for Centennial. That’s what this election is about: neighbors coming together, rolling up their sleeves, and doing the hard work to keep Centennial strong. We’ve walked the neighborhoods, knocked on doors, and met families across the city. And with every mile, our commitment has grown—not just to win an election, but to build a brighter future for the community we all love._
**[Ganahl’s “DougCo Dirty Dozen” puts union power on trial ahead of school board elections](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY JEN SCHUMANN | LOCAL | OCTOBER 28** With ballots out and school board races underway, Heidi Ganahl has posted six “Douglas County Dirty Dozen” videos asking one question—who sets priorities inside local classrooms? Her focus is the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) and four Douglas County candidates backed by $2,500 donations from AFT Colorado each—proof, she says, that national politics are steering local schools.

Goodman described herself as a “Truman Democrat” and said her decision was both personal and strategic—an effort to “mix up the landscape” in Republican-dominated rural Colorado by promoting liberty, fiscal restraint, and coalition-building within the Democratic Party. Goodman said she avoided the Republican Party because it’s “eating itself” and “can’t coalesce,” contrasting that with Democrats, whom she called “solid coalition builders.” | The Rocky Mountain Voice is a 501(c)(3) that exists to promote informed civic engagement and the principles of self-governance through enterprise reporting on public policy, politics, government, and culture throughout the state of Colorado. The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support! | CU Boulder student Nathaniel Ellis, a Turning Point USA leader, was struck in the head with a hockey stick by a masked skater who shouted “fascist,” an assault he believes was politically motivated. Prior to the attack, Antifa-linked social media accounts had labeled Ellis a “Nazi activist” and encouraged harassment, prompting him to report escalating threats. Boulder Police are investigating both the physical assault and the online harassment as potentially connected incidents; the suspect remains at large. | ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ BY MICHAEL HANCOCK | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 28 In October 1928, the Communist International — the Moscow-based command center for global revolution — issued an extraordinary directive. Buried in the archives of the Political Secretariat of the Communist International, the document was titled “Resolution on the Negro Question in the United States.” It did not read like a humanitarian plea to end racial injustice. It read like a military plan. BY ROBYN CARNES | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 28 Five candidates. Over 500 miles walked. One vision for Centennial. That’s what this election is about: neighbors coming together, rolling up their sleeves, and doing the hard work to keep Centennial strong. We’ve walked the neighborhoods, knocked on doors, and met families across the city. And with every mile, our commitment has grown—not just to win an election, but to build a brighter future for the community we all love. BY JEN SCHUMANN | LOCAL | OCTOBER 28 With ballots out and school board races underway, Heidi Ganahl has posted six “Douglas County Dirty Dozen” videos asking one question—who sets priorities inside local classrooms? Her focus is the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) and four Douglas County candidates backed by $2,500 donations from AFT Colorado each—proof, she says, that national politics are steering local schools. But the truth is, this is exactly who he's always been — a man who believes the rules don't apply to him. In just the past couple months alone, Donald deployed National Guard troops to patrol American streets and seized control of D.C.'s police force. He's pushing to ban mail-in voting and voting machines altogether to silence millions of voices. And his MAGA allies are rewriting congressional maps to steal elections and lock in Republican control for years to come. This is what authoritarianism looks like. It's happening right in front of our eyes, which is why I needed to write to you. I admire Jane Fonda more than I can say because she doesn’t just call out injustice, she acts. This has always been true. Her Climate PAC is one of the few organizations taking on two of the most powerful forces that define my uncle’s agenda: authoritarian politics and the fossil fuel industry that bankrolls him and thousands of candidates across the country. **But no one person can do this all alone. body:

Hey — it's Sarah.
**Do you have a sec to chat with me over the phone? 📞**
The reason I’m asking is that I’m planning on calling a few supporters who chip in to our campaign ahead of our October 31st end-of-month fundraising deadline on Friday.
[**Would you donate $5 or any amount you can afford today? I’ll be calling a handful of folks who chip in, and I’d love the opportunity to speak with you!**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20251029-1.Hitq1_&refcode=em20251029-2453&amount=5&t=2&akid=2453%2E21716%2ENsKQVU)

Don’t get me wrong. I love that you and I can communicate via email. These emails are one of the very best ways for us to stay connected about what I’m up to in Congress and all the progress we’re fighting for together here in Delaware.
**But there’s truly nothing like a good old-fashioned phone call, and I’d love the opportunity to connect with you to hear what’s on your mind.** I know too many folks in Delaware and across the country are worried about what’s ahead. **[I can’t wait to start calling a few members of this team who pitch in ahead of Friday’s fundraising deadline. We have to bring sanity and compassion back to Washington, and that starts with protecting the most critical seats in the nation, including WA-08. | | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

Hi Peter,
In case you didn’t already know, there may be an election coming up in your area on Tuesday, November 4th ( check here [https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/current-election.aspx] ), and this is your last weekend to vote! As we head into Halloween, we’re reminded that nothing is scarier than not taking part in our democracy. Stay safe from all the spooks this Halloween by casting your vote!
Have you made your plan to vote yet? If not, no worries! There are two ways to return your ballot:
1. Send it by mail! Your ballot must be postmarked on or before November 4th, and arrive at your county elections office within seven days of election day. And postage is prepaid!
2. Use an official dropbox [https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/drop-box-locator.aspx] ! As long as you are in line at an official dropbox location by 8pm on November 4th, your ballot will be accepted.
For any questions you may have about voting, take a look at our Voter Resources here [https://www.olcv.org/2025-voter-resources/] . If you need assistance voting or have further questions, contact your county elections office here [https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Pages/countyofficials.aspx] .
It’s more important than ever that we keep exercising our right to vote, so please take part in our democracy and get your ballot in!
Happy voting,

Your trust in me means the world.
Peter — I know that millions of people who are absolutely disgusted with Donald Trump’s presidency are looking to next month’s election to provide some hope.
I know that whether we win or lose — and believe me, it’s looking close — will set the tone for what comes next in 2026, 2028, and beyond.
I know that if we lose, Trump will just be emboldened to attack our institutions and our communities even more aggressively.
But I also know that if we win, we can start to turn the tide in a better direction. And that we will send a powerful message — to Donald Trump and to the entire country — that the American people do not accept the past nine months of cruelty and authoritarianism as our new normal.

Fellow patriot —

| | Hi, it’s Oregon Secretary of State, Tobias Read.
When President Trump’s Department of Justice demanded Oregon’s complete voter-registration data, including driver’s license numbers and parts of Social Security numbers. **I had one response:****No way! **
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/118252589/579153339/-1348697765?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkN2ZkZTZjZS0wM2I1LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=2U-p1YGY2oSO_KHZSuvCtKvqofgmhJOJYFaXJunusFc=&emci=63cd00c6-d9b4-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=d7fde6ce-03b5-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&ceid=30662126)

Oregon already provides the public voter information that’s required by law. **But private data belongs to Oregonians, not President Trump. Not to any President! ** My job is to protect both your right to vote and your right to privacy. **Donald Trump just endorsed my opponent Winsome Earle-Sears.**

The USDA has the power to stop this. They could use emergency authority to keep SNAP benefits flowing. They’ve used it before to protect WIC. They could do it again right now. And in just six days, we have two exciting opportunities to make that vision a reality. The first is in Virginia, where WFP-endorsed Ghazal Hashmi is running for Lt. Governor against MAGA-loyalist John Reid. Hashmi’s steadfast commitment to affordable housing, better jobs for working families, affordable health care, and more make her a candidate we’re beyond proud to stand beside. The second is in Cleveland, Ohio, where four WFP champions are up for election to the City Council — Rebecca Maurer, Mohammad Faraj, Alana Belle, and Tanmay Shah. This is our chance to bring fresh leadership to a city that tens of thousands of working families call home, and deliver improvements to Cleveland’s housing, public transit, public safety, and more. We’re hosting a string of phonebanks for these elections, and no matter where you live, we need your help. Races like these rarely get the attention they deserve, Peter. And we know it’s difficult to stay plugged into local issues while the national media machine is in overdrive. But in order to achieve the wins we need for working families across the country, we must show up everywhere — mayors, city councilors, state senators, lieutenant governors, and more. In solidarity, Team WFP Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. Reply directly to this email and let us know. This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. If you received this email as a forward and want to get the latest updates from the Working Families Party directly, The Working Families Party is the party of the multiracial working class, fighting for a nation that cares for all of us. | Friend -

# **Democrats waiver in shutdown siege, consider GOP proposal to pay federal workers**
Senate Democrats are **[examining a Republican proposal by Sen. Ron Johnson to pay all federal employees](https://substack.com/redirect/727e58e8-5f83-434b-9c84-252a3b77f2a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** --both essential workers required to report and furloughed workers--during the four-week government shutdown, with centrist Democrats like Mark Kelly and Tim Kaine saying they would take a "close look" at the measure.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/727e58e8-5f83-434b-9c84-252a3b77f2a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Growing pressure over SNAP benefits and food assistance:** Democrats plan to introduce legislation to fund SNAP benefits and the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children, as experts warn that more than 40 million Americans risk going hungry if benefits run out, with senators criticizing the Trump administration's refusal to spend emergency food assistance funds during the shutdown.
* **Federal workers union calls for clean resolution:** The American Federation of Government Employees, representing 820,000 federal workers, has called on Democrats to pass a clean continuing resolution to reopen the government, adding to pressure on Democratic leaders who publicly insist Trump must negotiate on health insurance subsidies before they agree to end the shutdown.
* **GOP leadership rejects piecemeal funding approach:** Vice President JD Vance urged Senate Republicans to maintain pressure on Democrats by rejecting "rifle-shot" measures to fund specific parts of government, arguing that passing such bills would relieve pressure on Democrats and potentially extend the shutdown, with Speaker Mike Johnson calling carve-out votes a "waste of our time."

* * *
# Massive crowds brave rain at ol' Miss ahead of TPUSA event featuring VP Vance and Erika Kirk
Vice President JD Vance will join Erika Kirk at a **[Turning Point USA event](https://substack.com/redirect/5cabe0da-e63a-47b9-803f-3789e0d635ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Wednesday at the University of Mississippi to honor Kirk's legacy of campus engagement.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4e67c3e4-0f0e-4911-861e-881372862aed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **First Campus Appearance since Assassination:** The free event at Ole Miss marks Erika Kirk's first campus tour appearance since her husband was assassinated on Sept. 10 during a debate at Utah Valley University, with Vance pledging to continue Kirk's mission of reaching young people through interactive Q&A sessions.
* **Hundreds Brave the Rain:** **Hundreds of students lined up** in the pouring rain earlier this afternoon to secure spots at the event, spanning across the university's campus with students adorned in pro-America attire.
* **Where to Watch:** Fox News will broadcast the 5 p.m. CT gathering live on "Jesse Watters Primetime" and stream it on Fox Nation, followed by a behind-the-scenes documentary series premiere on Nov. 7.

* * *
# **Putin announces successful test of nuclear 'Tsunami' torpedo**
Russian President Vladimir Putin announced Wednesday that his military successfully tested the Poseidon nuclear torpedo, an **[underwater weapon designed to trigger radioactive tsunamis](https://substack.com/redirect/701b38e1-10d3-4809-8e6c-617c58eab051?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** up to 1,600 feet high capable of devastating coastal cities.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/701b38e1-10d3-4809-8e6c-617c58eab051?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Putin told wounded Russian soldiers** at a Moscow hospital that the submarine-launched test was a "huge success," marking the first time Russia launched both the torpedo's engine and its nuclear power unit, claiming the weapon's destructive power exceeds even the Sarmat "Satan II" intercontinental ballistic missile.
* **The Poseidon** is estimated to carry a 2-megaton warhead with more than 150 times the power of the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima in 1945, and is designed to trigger massive radioactive tsunamis from hundreds of miles away, according to Russian state media.
* **The test follows Putin 's recent nuclear drill** and Sunday's confirmation of a successful Burevestnik cruise missile test, with both weapons announced in 2018 as Russia's response to U.S. withdrawal from the 1972 Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty and NATO expansion.
* * *

# Harvard hosts panel on bipartisanship with completely partisan panel
A Harvard University panel billed as a discussion on bridging the partisan divide featured **[only left-wing participants](https://substack.com/redirect/87af2afe-e212-4948-b515-caff72b45a70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , including two former Democratic officials and the NAACP president, raising questions about the university's commitment to ideological balance.
* **Across the Divide?** : The Oct. 9 event titled "Across the Divide: Organizing to Build Bridges in Partisan Times" included former Democratic Rep. Joe Kennedy, former New Orleans Mayor Mitch Landrieu, and NAACP President Derrick Johnson, who used the platform to criticize President Trump, defend DEI programs, and call the current political climate a "national crisis in our democracy."
* **Bipartisan Posers:** Panelists made partisan statements including calling Secretary of War Pete Hegseth "a DEI hire" and claiming "anti-democracy forces" in Republican-leaning regions threaten voting rights and democratic freedom, while Kennedy's organization describes its mission as combating these forces in the Deep South and Appalachia.
* **Harvard Stands its Ground:** Harvard Kennedy School defended the event by noting it hosts speakers from across the political spectrum, including recent appearances by conservatives such as Jared Kushner, Kellyanne Conway, Mike Pence, and Nikki Haley, stating that students must learn to engage across partisan lines even if specific events may appear "unbalanced."

* * *
# Left social media influencer turned congressional candidate faces criminal charges
A Democratic congressional candidate and former Media Matters employee has been **[federally indicted](https://substack.com/redirect/5a828f14-7192-482a-814c-0ce527560543?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for allegedly impeding immigration enforcement during a September protest outside a Chicago-area ICE facility.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b5602511-371f-4ed9-9cb2-46c411d913d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **The Charges:** Kat Abughazaleh, 26, and co-defendants were charged with conspiring to prevent federal law enforcement from carrying out official duties by forming a human chain that blocked an ICE vehicle at the Broadview, Illinois facility on Sept. 26, forcing the officer to drive at extremely slow speeds to avoid injuring protesters.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9142ad19-9d68-4bbb-a466-44968bde446f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Congressional Race** : Abughazaleh is running for Illinois' Ninth Congressional District in a crowded March primary field, seeking to replace retiring 81-year-old Democratic Rep. Jan Schakowsky.
* **Influencer Hates Consequences:** The candidate denounced the Oct. 23 indictment as "political prosecution" aimed at criminalizing protest and silencing dissent, claiming ICE has violently attacked hundreds of protesters and accusing the Trump administration of "unhinged and unlawful tactics" while vowing to continue fighting what she called America's "backslide into fascism."

body:
Besides its lengthy history of incompetence, the federal agency
created by Jimmy Carter to provide the nation with disaster relief
singled out conservative victims and withheld aid to survivors who
displayed signs and flags the agency’s liberal workforce disagreed
with, including those supporting President Trump.

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77445&L=36355&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZmVtYS13aXRoaGVsZC1kaXNhc3Rlci1haWQvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPWNvcnJ1cHRpb24rY2hyb25pY2xlcyZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=1e5e66e4a0dc8a208f51b22f445f15ea42cb07ff2a09d1c22cb78421e15080f6]

Besides its lengthy history of incompetence, the federal agency
created by Jimmy Carter to provide the nation with disaster relief
singled out conservative victims and withheld aid to survivors who
displayed signs and flags the agency’s liberal workforce disagreed
with, including those supporting President Trump. The “textbook
political discrimination against Americans in crisis” was uncovered
by a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) investigation that found
throughout the Biden administration the Federal Emergency Management
Agency (FEMA)—charged with helping people before, during and after
disasters—systemically refused to visit the houses of politically
conservative victims.

**Hey folks, Cliff here.**
And I'll tell you right off the bat--this one was special. Today, [David Shuster](https://open.substack.com/users/16891317-david-shuster?utm_source=mentions) and I had the great honor of talking with Michigan's _**Lieutenant Governor[Garlin Gilchrist II](https://open.substack.com/users/353055019-garlin-gilchrist-ii?utm_source=mentions)**_, a guy I've known for nearly two decades, back from our days at Brave New Films.
Even then, you could tell--this was someone built for leadership, for problem-solving, for _building_ things that matter. And sure enough, Garlin's gone from tech visionary to public servant, and now he's running to be the next Governor of Michigan.
**Let me be blunt** :_I 've already endorsed him. _
Because this guy has both the brains _and_ the backbone, the charisma and courage we need to defend democracy. When we asked why he was running his immediate answer was like sweet music to our ears: [He's fighting Trump, Trump's attacks on good policy, decency, taste, Trump's very persona](https://substack.com/redirect/8f9242c1-9454-4e00-838b-a12cdc59e0dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and his piss cotton candy hair.
Ok, I added that last one myself.
Garlin doesn't want to send stern letters to a Trumpian wrecking crew hellbent on tearing Michigan--and America--apart. He will be wherever the fight is--in person.
Garlin's not a soundbite politician--he's an engineer, literally, and he approaches government like a system that can and must be fixed.
* * *
Find great candidates like Garlin--subscribe!
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.AlKbpV7ZhuMJXfe_tKwU1b25RPqXreB9zsDrHH1Y2yM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=177490035)
* * *
He's stood shoulder-to-shoulder with Gretchen Whitmer, helping deliver record education funding, repeal Michigan's right-to-work law, and restore dignity to working people across his state. And now he's running to finish the job--protect progress, expand opportunity, [and stand up to the billionaire bullies who've turned public policy into their personal playground](https://substack.com/redirect/26410dcc-5681-4a76-9720-fd41e3dba738?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Go see for yourself what he's about--and if you can, chip in a few bucks at **[GarlinGilchrist.com](https://substack.com/redirect/faaeb6f5-b755-4f32-832a-4e5f46512d04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. The average donation to his campaign is just $24. That's how real movements get built.
David, as always, brought the thunder--this time not just with sharp questions, but also a reminder that he recently _rewrote_ Edgar Allan Poe's _The Raven_ as a searing takedown of Trump's grotesque reign. It's up on our Substack, and if you haven't read it yet, trust me--you're missing brilliance.

[We talked with ](https://substack.com/redirect/dae6d0a7-92e0-431f-aa52-9df4d4c7d843?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Nina Burleigh](https://substack.com/redirect/dae6d0a7-92e0-431f-aa52-9df4d4c7d843?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ about the deep rot and corruption that enabled Jeffrey Epstein's empire of abuse](https://substack.com/redirect/dae6d0a7-92e0-431f-aa52-9df4d4c7d843?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and with **[Dana DuBois](https://substack.com/redirect/2e07a5f9-6cce-4725-b48b-436190596e5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ of ](https://substack.com/redirect/2e07a5f9-6cce-4725-b48b-436190596e5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[genXy](https://substack.com/redirect/2e07a5f9-6cce-4725-b48b-436190596e5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ about the fight to preserve truth, equity, and sanity in a world that seems hell-bent on losing all three](https://substack.com/redirect/2e07a5f9-6cce-4725-b48b-436190596e5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
These conversations aren't random--they're the building blocks of what Blue Amp Media _is_ and what we're trying to build: a platform for truth, courage, and [resistance against the rising tide of fascism](https://substack.com/redirect/8f9242c1-9454-4e00-838b-a12cdc59e0dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), so we can get rid of _this guy_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8f9242c1-9454-4e00-838b-a12cdc59e0dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Gyeongju, South Korea. REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein
Because here's the deal, friends: we're not just running a show--**we 're building a movement**. One that connects people who refuse to give up on democracy, who still believe character and compassion matter, who understand that decency is not weakness--it's strength--and who get that fighting is about doing what it takes to win--whether it's an election, a policy, a legal battle, a huge protest, civil disobedience or [just embarrassing Trump's lackeys by sending them knee pads](https://substack.com/redirect/8f9242c1-9454-4e00-838b-a12cdc59e0dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

body:
I need to tell you what President Trump is doing. There is a hunger crisis rapidly growing in our country. **42 million Americans are about to lose their SNAP benefits on November 1st because of Donald Trump and his Republican majority that forced a government shutdown.** To make matters worse, Trump literally just sent $20 billion to bail out Argentina, while letting millions of Americans go hungry. clean_body: That’s how important it is. | A LETTER FROM THE DESK OF THE HOUSE GOP LEADERSHIP CHAIR, REP. ELISE STEFANIK Friend, I know you probably get bombarded with fundraising emails. Believe me, I get them myself! But this is no ordinary email. The stakes are far greater – New York is literally on the brink of a communist takeover! In fact, if you only read through one of these emails all year, it should be this one. That’s how important it is! Please allow me to explain... On November 4th, voters in New York City are about to go to the polls to elect their next mayor. The Democrat nominee – and the current frontrunner – is radical communist Zohran Mamdani. I could go into detail about how he’s a devout Marxist, a Muslim jihadist, and a virulent antisemite. How he’s campaigned with Hamas supporters and terrorist sympathizers. How he’s described violence as “an artificial construction,” called for prisons to be abolished, supported defunding the police, and even stated that his end goal is “seizing the means of production.” I could tell you about his disastrous agenda and how it would devastate New York. Cripplingly high taxes, releasing criminals from prison, protecting illegals from ICE, and even state-run grocery stores are all part of his plans for our state. I could tell you about the advice and guidance he’s getting from Obama’s political machine. How they see him as the “next Obama”. I could tell you about how our current governor, Kathy Hochul, has endorsed Mamdani, campaigned by his side, and all but promised to rubber stamp his entire far Left agenda. But at this point, I trust you’ve heard enough about Mamdani’s dangerous plans for New York. What’s most important now is that we come together to SAVE New York by defeating Mamdani at the final hour and then FIRING his enabler Kathy Hochul! Last year, you stood with President Trump as we fought – and won – the final battle for America. Now, as the senior elected Republican here in the Empire State, I’m asking that you stand with me to fight – and win – the final battle to SAVE New York. The last end-of-month deadline before Election Day is on October 31st. When the clock strikes midnight, we’ll need to have raised another $78,484 to reach our budget for final, critical days of the election. Our only hope of doing that is through the support for grassroots conservatives like YOU. Everything we’ve been fighting for this year is hanging in the balance. All our hard work, the millions we’ve raised, the sacrifices we’ve made – it was all for this moment. That is why I’ve authorized one final 500% MATCH before the deadline to ensure your grassroots contributions go as far as possible at the final hour. All I can do now is pray that you’ll take advantage. Thank you, Rep. Elise Stefanik Paid for by Team Elise, a joint fundraising committee authorized by and composed of Elise for Congress and E-PAC. www.elisestefanik.com PO Box 500 Glens Falls, NY 12801

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.
---

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

Our plan to fight for fair elections with fair representation: |

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/118260831/579181398/1793776944?refcode=bsc_emm_ffa_20251029_T1_LGWonSCOTUS_v1s2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhMTNiYjk1Yi0xZGI1LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hyRVUuKUfmTHOjnrmXJ7g2YYZyFAilxKBcs9fmO28bk=&emci=993bb95b-1db5-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=a13bb95b-1db5-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&ceid=1037277)

| | Team, The Supreme Court has signaled the direction it may be about to take. Now the rest is up to us. The Court recently heard new oral arguments in _Louisiana v. Callais_ , and questions from the bench suggest that **the far-right majority may dismantle Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act,** which protects against racially discriminatory redistricting. According to a new analysis from Fair Fight Action and the Black Voters Matter Fund, if the Court strikes down Section 2, Republicans could gain 19 new safe U.S. House seats. It would gut representation for Black and Brown Americans and be enough to lock in one-party control of the House for a generation. But we have a path forward. 1\. With this team’s grassroots support, we are **conducting a massive communications and mobilization effort** pushing the Court to uphold the Voting Rights Act. 2\. But because a ruling could come by the beginning of next year, we’re already **preparing for the whole South to be drawing new maps in early 2026.** 3\. **We’ll fight for fair representation** with mass mobilization at state capitols and federal buildings, strategic pressure campaigns, coordinated and strategic action with litigation groups, and state-level organizing. 4\. And for the long haul, we’ll keep pushing Congress to investigate unfair maps, expose corruption, confront a Supreme Court that’s abandoned its duty to the Constitution, and pass reforms like the Freedom to Vote Act and the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, which would **restore federal voting protections and outlaw the extreme gerrymandering fueling this crisis.** [**This moment demands action, and we’re counting on this team’s support to power this work. Peter -

I'm sitting down to write to you today with a heart full of gratitude and a spirit that's more fired up than ever. Since announcing my run for Governor of Virginia, the outpouring of support has been nothing short of incredible.

I've received thousands of messages from folks all across the Commonwealth - It's humbling to have the prayers and support of so many patriots.

As a Marine and a proud conservative, I know that I have the experience and the conviction to lead our great Commonwealth forward. I'm committed to protecting the promise of Virginia, where every child can get a world-class education, every business can thrive, and every family can live in safety and prosperity.

But I didn't expect the rush of enthusiasm that's swept across our campaign. _**From the bottom of my heart, thank you for being part of this movement.**_ Your encouragement, your volunteer hours, and your generous financial support are the fuel that will propel us ever forward.

clean_body: That’s how important it is. | A LETTER FROM THE DESK OF THE HOUSE GOP LEADERSHIP CHAIR, REP. ELISE STEFANIK Friend, I know you probably get bombarded with fundraising emails. Believe me, I get them myself! But this is no ordinary email. The stakes are far greater – New York is literally on the brink of a communist takeover! In fact, if you only read through one of these emails all year, it should be this one. That’s how important it is! Please allow me to explain... On November 4th, voters in New York City are about to go to the polls to elect their next mayor. The Democrat nominee – and the current frontrunner – is radical communist Zohran Mamdani. I could go into detail about how he’s a devout Marxist, a Muslim jihadist, and a virulent antisemite. How he’s campaigned with Hamas supporters and terrorist sympathizers. How he’s described violence as “an artificial construction,” called for prisons to be abolished, supported defunding the police, and even stated that his end goal is “seizing the means of production.” I could tell you about his disastrous agenda and how it would devastate New York. Cripplingly high taxes, releasing criminals from prison, protecting illegals from ICE, and even state-run grocery stores are all part of his plans for our state. I could tell you about the advice and guidance he’s getting from Obama’s political machine. How they see him as the “next Obama”. I could tell you about how our current governor, Kathy Hochul, has endorsed Mamdani, campaigned by his side, and all but promised to rubber stamp his entire far Left agenda. But at this point, I trust you’ve heard enough about Mamdani’s dangerous plans for New York. What’s most important now is that we come together to SAVE New York by defeating Mamdani at the final hour and then FIRING his enabler Kathy Hochul! Last year, you stood with President Trump as we fought – and won – the final battle for America. Now, as the senior elected Republican here in the Empire State, I’m asking that you stand with me to fight – and win – the final battle to SAVE New York. The last end-of-month deadline before Election Day is on October 31st. When the clock strikes midnight, we’ll need to have raised another $78,484 to reach our budget for final, critical days of the election. Our only hope of doing that is through the support for grassroots conservatives like YOU. Everything we’ve been fighting for this year is hanging in the balance. All our hard work, the millions we’ve raised, the sacrifices we’ve made – it was all for this moment. That is why I’ve authorized one final 500% MATCH before the deadline to ensure your grassroots contributions go as far as possible at the final hour. All I can do now is pray that you’ll take advantage. Thank you, Rep. Elise Stefanik Paid for by Team Elise, a joint fundraising committee authorized by and composed of Elise for Congress and E-PAC. www.elisestefanik.com PO Box 500 Glens Falls, NY 12801

body:
Republican cruelty forces Americans to choose between their own health and making rent
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=1932%2E791427%2Ek0kbc-)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-oct25.q9Ch2B&refcode=em251029-1-180&t=2&akid=1932%2E791427%2Ek0kbc-)
Friend — We’re about to be 30 days into this government shutdown, and it’s important to remember why we’re here.
Trump and Republicans are set to cut funding that helps bring down the cost of health care plans under the Affordable Care Act. Democrats stepped up to defend Americans from skyrocketing premiums and millions losing their coverage. Republicans have spent 30 days refusing to negotiate or even consider finding a solution to this health care crisis that they created.
Let’s put those cuts in perspective. **24 million** Americans are currently getting their health insurance through the ACA, and all are in danger of seeing hikes to their premiums come 2026.
One of those Americans is Jessica from Florida. The Wall Street Journal reports that her health insurance premiums will jump from around $200 a month to **$1,100** a month if the Republicans’ planned cuts go through.
Those costs are so high that Jessica may just become one of the 4 million Americans that experts estimate will be forced off their ACA plans. That would be devastating, given that Jessica regularly sees a specialist for an eye condition and may in the future require surgery to avoid blindness.
**This is how Republican cruelty forces Americans to choose between their own health and making rent.**
And let’s not forget that Republicans already got away with a massive health care cut this year when they passed their Big Beautiful Bill. They stole almost a trillion dollars from Medicaid funds so they could pay for massive tax cuts for billionaires. Now over 11 million more Americans will lose their health care over the coming years, and costs will rise for millions more.
Friend, Ilhan Omar understands that there is only one antidote to Trump and the GOP’s disastrous agenda on health care: Medicare-for-All.
It is outrageous that America is the wealthiest nation in the history of the world, but is the only developed nation that does not provide health care as a human right.
Ilhan is committed to not only holding the line on opposing cuts to the ACA, but also to working every day to build the movement for Medicare-for-All and a future where Americans get the health care they deserve, no matter their income.

But if you can afford it, please chip in $10 or any amount to support Ilhan’s campaign to protect Americans from insanely high health care costs come 2026, and to finally pass Medicare-for-All and guarantee health care as a right for all people.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-oct25.q9Ch2B&refcode=em251029-1-180&t=3&akid=1932%2E791427%2Ek0kbc-)

clean_body: Republican cruelty forces Americans to choose between their own health and making rent - - Friend — We’re about to be 30 days into this government shutdown, and it’s important to remember why we’re here. Trump and Republicans are set to cut funding that helps bring down the cost of health care plans under the Affordable Care Act. Democrats stepped up to defend Americans from skyrocketing premiums and millions losing their coverage. Republicans have spent 30 days refusing to negotiate or even consider finding a solution to this health care crisis that they created. Let’s put those cuts in perspective. 24 million Americans are currently getting their health insurance through the ACA, and all are in danger of seeing hikes to their premiums come 2026. One of those Americans is Jessica from Florida. The Wall Street Journal reports that her health insurance premiums will jump from around $200 a month to $1,100 a month if the Republicans’ planned cuts go through. Those costs are so high that Jessica may just become one of the 4 million Americans that experts estimate will be forced off their ACA plans. That would be devastating, given that Jessica regularly sees a specialist for an eye condition and may in the future require surgery to avoid blindness. This is how Republican cruelty forces Americans to choose between their own health and making rent. And let’s not forget that Republicans already got away with a massive health care cut this year when they passed their Big Beautiful Bill. They stole almost a trillion dollars from Medicaid funds so they could pay for massive tax cuts for billionaires. Now over 11 million more Americans will lose their health care over the coming years, and costs will rise for millions more. Friend, Ilhan Omar understands that there is only one antidote to Trump and the GOP’s disastrous agenda on health care: Medicare-for-All. It is outrageous that America is the wealthiest nation in the history of the world, but is the only developed nation that does not provide health care as a human right. Ilhan is committed to not only holding the line on opposing cuts to the ACA, but also to working every day to build the movement for Medicare-for-All and a future where Americans get the health care they deserve, no matter their income. - If you've saved payment info with ActBlue Express, your contribution will go through immediately: | | - | - | | - | - | | - | - In solidarity, Team Ilhan PAID FOR BY ILHAN FOR CONGRESS

---
| **Dear Friend,** I’m reaching out personally because our campaign for re‐election is at a critical moment, and I need your support. Serving as your Congressman for North Carolina’s 8th District has been one of the greatest honors of my life, and I’m determined to keep fighting for our families, our freedoms, and our future. **Right now, hardworking Americans are being hurt by the ongoing Federal Shutdown caused by Senate Democrats and Chuck Schumer’s political games.** Families are struggling, government workers are unsure if they’ll get paid, and vital services are being disrupted — all because leadership in Washington is putting politics ahead of people. **I’ve been speaking out against this, and I will continue to fight to end the shutdown and hold those responsible accountable.**
---
| **But I can’t do this alone. The opposition is already raising big money and organizing hard**. To compete and win, we need resources for outreach, communications, and voter engagement. Every contribution, no matter the size, helps us fight back against the obstruction in Washington and keep North Carolina’s values represented in Congress. **Will you make a contribution of $100, $50, $25, or even $10 today to help me continue this fight?**
---

---
| I am proud to serve this district, and I promise to keep standing for our values, our communities, and our future.

Thank you for standing with us,

Mark Harris
